_comment: tools/bm_vault_provenance.py entered the inventory on 2026-08-31 (WBS row VB3-07, enterprise evidence locators: query_id, document_span, capture): three sys.stderr.write sites, all operator-facing and none carrying user or model text. Two are in get-evidence and its note-resolution helper, printing NO-DATA or UNKNOWN-ASSERTION naming the --note/--claim arguments the caller themselves typed on the command line. The third is _read_jsonl warning that one line of a caller-supplied --query-ledger fixture file was not valid JSON, naming only the line number and the parser exception text, mirroring bm_vault_cite.py._read_citations, an already-reviewed site of the same shape. bm_vault_labels.py entered the inventory on 2026-08-31 (VB3-13, derived memory cannot declassify) with 3 write sites, all inside propagate(): the temp-then-os.replace atomic write of a derived note's own frontmatter fields (security_label, derived_from_labels tightened forward) when a source note is relabeled more restrictive. No user or model prose is written, only vocabulary values this module itself defines (LABELS) and ids/paths already present in the vault; reviewed site by site, not accepted on the scanner's count alone. tools/bm_vault_identity.py entered the inventory on 2026-08-31 (VB3-17, opaque ids, tenant as a field, merge history as events) with 3 write sites, all inside append_event(): os.makedirs of the .identity directory, the os.open(O_APPEND|O_CREAT|O_WRONLY) of events.jsonl, and the os.write of one JSON line. No user or model prose is written, only opaque entity ids already validated as vault note ids, a rule-version string the caller typed on the command line, and ISO dates; reviewed site by site, not accepted on the scanner's count alone. bm_vault_jbench.py landed at 4 on 2026-08-31 (VB2-03, the Japanese-first retrieval benchmark runner): os.makedirs and a write-mode open for its own temp-directory user-dictionary.json (installed once per run so dictionary_dependent cases exercise the analyzer seam real dictionary path, never a tracked file), the json.dump call writing through that same handle, and shutil.rmtree cleaning up its own temp vault directory afterward. No user or model text reaches any of them: the dictionary terms come from the benchmark fixture file and the vault directory is deleted, never read back by anything else. Seven sites entered on 2026-09-01 (silent-failure lint debt closure, hub branch wbs/lint-debt-silent-failures), reviewed site by site: bm_forecast.py +1 (a malformed recorded_at now warns naming the task id before the documented degrade-to-0.0), bm_vault_audit.py +1 (a row with an unparseable ts under a since/until filter warns, mirroring the file's existing skipping-malformed-line site), bm_vault_cli.py +2 (a failed git reset after refused apply warns with a status --short pointer, twice, once per reset site), bm_vault_enrich.py +1 and bm_vault_labels.py +2 and bm_vault_temporal.py +1 (an unreadable note during a scan warns naming the path and OSError text instead of vanishing from the scan). Every one of the seven prints only a module-prefixed diagnostic naming a path, task id, or OS exception; no user or model prose reaches any of them. tools/bm_vault_lint.py moved from 4 to 5 on 2026-09-04 (the created/id derivation feature, commit 66ca4ff8): the new site is the atomic --apply write inside _apply_fix (open(tmp, "w"), fh.write(new_text), os.replace(tmp, path), three calls the scanner already counted as one site group before, now two more stderr.write sites from the same function's git-log failure warnings are counted individually by the widened scanner). No user or model prose is written: only frontmatter field values derived from the vault's own git history (a date) or a sha256 of the note's own path (an id), and the stderr lines name only a relative path and the underlying OSError text. tools/vault_recall_hook.py moved from 3 to 4 on 2026-09-04: the index-age stderr.write in cmd_check (the E54 status-line, printed once per session beside the unconfigured refusal) was added without updating this count. All four sites are operator-facing diagnostics or a local once-per-session marker file (SEEN, an append of a session:path key), never user or model prose. tools/bm_repo_scope.py entered the inventory on 2026-09-04 (E76, per-repository hook scoping): 5 write sites. Two are the file-system writes inside _notice_pending (os.makedirs of .brothermode/repo-scope-notice, then an O_CREAT|O_EXCL os.open of one per-session marker file whose content is empty and whose one path segment is a sha256 hash of the session id, mirroring bm_fence_hook.py's ensure_token). The other three are sys.stderr.write calls in hooks_off: the garbage-config diagnostic (names the config path and the OSError/UnicodeDecodeError text, never file content), the fixed NOTICE sentence (a hardcoded string, no interpolation), and the top-level fail-open diagnostic (names an exception type and message). None carries user or model prose, only operator-facing diagnostics and a hardcoded sentence, the same shape already reviewed for the sibling hooks' own stderr sites. tools/bm_vault_decay.py entered the inventory on 2026-09-04 (readiness row E57 mechanism 2, time decay and reinforcement over the recall ranking, borrowed from MemoryBank, https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10250) with 5 write sites, all of them inside write_store(): the os.makedirs of the store's parent directory, the os.fdopen of a temp file in that same directory, the json.dump through that handle, the os.replace that installs it atomically, and the os.remove that cleans the temp file up when a write raised. No user or model text reaches any of them: the store holds note slugs (already vault note filenames) mapped to an integer repetition count and a float unix timestamp, nothing else. Nothing in that module writes to a vault note at all, which is the constitution's own line and the reason the store is a sidecar rather than a frontmatter field. tools/vault_recall_hook.py moved from 4 to 6 on the same row (mechanism 1, the outcome number beside the mechanism, borrowed from MemOS, https://github.com/MemTensor/MemOS): the two added sites are _append_outcome()'s append-mode open of the shared hook-outcome log and its single json.dumps write. No recalled note text and no model prose is written there: the numbers are counted FROM the recalled text and the text itself never leaves the frame, which is what keeps a poisoned note out of a second file. scripts/doctor.py moved from 6 to 10 on 2026-09-04 (battery round 25 repairs): blocked_write_simulation() now opts its own throwaway project in the way bm_repo_scope requires before it can measure the fence at all, so the four added sites are two os.makedirs (.git and .brother inside the mkdtemp this function already deletes), the write-mode io.open of .brother/config, and the fh.write of one hardcoded comment line into it. No user or model text reaches any of them: the only content written is a fixed English sentence this file holds as a literal, and every path is inside the temporary directory the function removes when it returns. LL-1 (2026-09-05, the attempt breaker ships in every install): three new tools/ modules copied from scripts/ (the same one-source, byte-identical-copy law brother_paths.py already follows), reviewed site by site. tools/attempt_hook.py lands at 6: two are _append_outcome()'s append-mode open of the shared hook-outcome log and its one json.dumps write, the identical mechanism vault_recall_hook.py's own entry above already covers (a count, never recalled or model text); the other four are sys.stderr.write calls carrying only this module's own fixed English sentences plus, where a value is interpolated, an OS exception's type name and message (a ledger write failure, a malformed-stdin parse failure) or the ledger's own store path, the same line-number-and-parser-exception shape bm_vault_cite.py._read_citations already established above as reviewed. tools/attempt_ledger.py lands at 1: record()'s own fh.write of one JSON line into the local attempt ledger, carrying the fingerprinted technique class (home path collapsed, numbers and hashes replaced with a placeholder, never the literal command) and up to 500 characters of the failing command's own stderr or stdout tail. That text is the ledger's entire purpose, exactly as much as the command that produced it already exists in the transcript, and it never leaves the local ledger file this mechanism exists to populate. tools/pattern_note.py lands at 4: write()'s two with-open/write pairs (the note file itself and the index line appended beside it), both AFTER gate_text()'s call into bm_vault_intake.hard_gate (credential_hit then deny_list_hit), the same credential and deny-list gate admit and capture already run before any vault write, so nothing reaches either file ungated. scripts/find_out.py copied at the same time writes nothing (it only reads and prints) and carries no entry here. tools/bm_profile.py enters the inventory on 2026-09-05 (V7, the vault profile) with 5 write sites, all inside record(): os.makedirs of the profile's parent directory, the append-mode open, the fixed header text written once on first use, the dated key/value line itself, and the sys.stderr.write in _read_text's OSError branch naming only a path and the exception text. record()'s key and value are the operator's own stated facts (role, level, a preference), the same "caller themselves typed on the command line" shape bm_vault_provenance.py's entry above already established as reviewed; no user or model prose reaches either write. tools/bm_vault.py moved from 9 to 10 on 2026-09-05 (commit 8c379a3e, V5 the immutable hash-chained read-audit trail): the new site is a sys.stderr.write in recall's read-audit call naming only the caught exception text ("read audit unavailable (%s); recall continues"), the same shape every other "mechanism unavailable, continuing" diagnostic in this file already carries. No user or model prose reaches it. tools/bm_vault_cli.py moved from 13 to 22 on 2026-09-05 (commit 1bf291f8c, the bind verb): the nine new sites are all inside cmd_bind, which writes only {"vault": PATH} merged into bm_vault.py's own config, atomically (temp file then os.replace). PATH is the directory the caller named on the command line; every stdout/stderr site names only that path, the usage string, or a caught OSError's text. No user or model prose reaches any of the nine, the same "caller themselves typed on the command line" shape already reviewed above. tools/bm_vault_heat_temporal.py enters the inventory on 2026-09-05 with 10 write sites: five are sys.stderr.write diagnostics naming only a note path and a caught OSError/ValueError text (an unreadable note, a malformed frontmatter field, a corrupt heat file starting empty); the other five are _save_heat's own atomic write (os.makedirs, the temp-file open, json.dump, its trailing newline, os.replace). The heat file holds only note ids (already-validated vault note filenames) mapped to a plain integer recall count, the same note-slug-to-count sidecar shape bm_vault_decay.py's entry above already established as reviewed. No user or model prose reaches any of the ten. tools/bm_vault_read_audit.py enters the inventory on 2026-09-05 (V5, the immutable hash-chained read-audit trail) with 7 write sites: two sys.stderr.write NO-DATA diagnostics (an unparseable chain tail, a caught OSError), one unknown-command diagnostic naming only the argument the caller typed, one usage line, and append()'s own os.makedirs/os.open(O_APPEND|O_CREAT|O_WRONLY, 0o600)/os.write of one hash-chained JSON row. The row holds only a note id or path (never its content), a fixed caller-surface name, a session id, and a query's sha256, exactly as append()'s own docstring states ("only its sha256 is ever written to disk"); the same access-record shape bm_vault_audit.py's entry above already established as reviewed. No user or model prose reaches any of the seven. tools/bm_vault_retier.py enters the inventory on 2026-09-06 (P0.1, the one-time re-tag tool for legacy vault notes under the strict-withhold flip) with 3 write sites, all inside apply_plan and main: the write-mode open of a vault note being re-tagged, its own fh.write of the note's new bytes (the original text plus two or three new frontmatter lines: status, retiered_at, and an evidence_locator only when one already resolves), and a sys.stderr.write NO-DATA diagnostic naming only a nonexistent --vault-root path. The bytes written to a note are never model or session prose: they are the note's own existing text unchanged plus fixed field names, today's date, and a relative path already present on disk, the same operator-facing shape every entry above already establishes as reviewed. tools/bm_vault.py moved from 10 to 11 on 2026-09-06 (Row P0-M, the loud disabled-seam banner): the new site is a sys.stderr.write in cmd_check printing bm_vault_seams.banner() once per run, before anything else, naming every disabled seam so a mutation seam can never run silently even if nobody reads the hit lines below. The banner text is a fixed, module-authored sentence per disabled seam name, never user or model prose, the same operator-facing diagnostic shape every stderr.write entry above already establishes as reviewed.
